messages:
opsbot: [ALERT] Smart routing: fallback loop detected for customer=nimbus-prod across regions us-east-1 -> us-west-2 (retries=3, obs_errors=6.8%). Link: https://internal/redwood/incidents/1893001234

maria: @jin paging — seeing elevated 5xx and token-dropping errors starting ~11:07 UTC. First noticed on rdx-7b-q4f in us-east-1. Latency x3 for affected customers. :rotating_light:

jin: I'm oncall. looking at logs now. quick ask: was there any manual routing or model pin in the last hour?

dan: I pushed an emergency force-model pin at 11:12 to route heavy customers to rdx-ggml-7b as a short-term throughput mitigation. I left a note in #eng-runtime.

maria: that was likely the trigger — the pin bypassed the usual capacity checks. ops graphs show a sharp drop in available slots in us-east-1 immediately after.

jin: log excerpt:
```
2026-03-15T11:13:02Z [runtime] route_eval: policy=smart_route_v2 decision=force_pin model=rdx-ggml-7b region=us-east-1
2026-03-15T11:13:05Z [runtime] kvcache: miss -> warmup triggered
2026-03-15T11:13:07Z [inference] error: incompatible-kv-cache, dropping request
```

sara: PagerDuty escalated a page to SRE at 11:18. Customer success (Alex) on the call; multiple customers reported completion failures for long generations.

alex-cs: Customer Nimbus reports ~30% of calls failing with partial outputs. They're threatening to revert to another provider if this persists. Need ETA.

jin: I'm going to roll back Dan's force-pin to restore normal routing. Command I will run:
```bash
rictl routing rollback --id force-pin-20260315-1112 --reason "mitigation caused capacity exhaustion"
```

dan: if you rollback, note that we lose the temporary throughput improvement. but agree it's causing more harm.

opsbot: action: rollback initiated by jin at 11:22 UTC; previous policy state saved as snap-20260315-1120.

jen: (typo, meant jin) rolling back now...

jin: rollback completed at 11:23 but now I'm seeing a region fallback churn: requests started failing in us-east-1 so router redirected to us-west-2, which then hit its own capacity and started falling back to tiny-quant model variants, producing high token-drop errors. This is the loop opsbot detected.

maria: sequence of events looks like: manual force -> capacity exhausted -> rollback -> routing engine tries cross-region -> us-west-2 overload -> fallback to incompatible variant -> increased errors. Bad interaction between force-pin and fallback heuristics.

dan: oh — I also had a manual temporary quota bump on the dedicated pool in us-west-2 that expired at 11:20; that combined with rollback timing explains the sudden pressure.

pagerduty-bot: Escalation: incident severity set to P0 at 11:25. Paging SRE and Runtime.

jin: immediate mitigation plan: 1) pause cross-region failover for the affected customer (lock routing to origin region to stop churn), 2) raise dedicated pool capacity in us-west-2 to absorb spill, 3) revert any expired quota policies, 4) coordinate customer-facing comms.

commands I'm running now:
```bash
# 1) lock routing for Nimbus back to origin region
rictl routing lock --customer nimbus-prod --region us-east-1 --ttl 10m --reason "stop fallback churn"
# 2) scale dedicated pool in us-west-2
rictl capacity scale --pool dedicated-us-west-2 --delta +4
```

maria: I'll open a short status page banner and ping CS to prepare a mitigation note. alex-cs, pls prepare a draft.

alex-cs: Draft: "We’re investigating increased errors affecting some long-generation requests. We’ve applied mitigations; we will follow up within 30 minutes with status and ETA."

jin: locks in place at 11:29, capacity scaled at 11:30. Observability: error rate trending down but latency still elevated. No additional customer-impacting failures in the last 5m.

dan: we should also patch the routing policy to avoid honoring force-pins that bypass capacity checks in the future. That logic chain is dangerous. I'll open a PR after incident.

maria: postmortem checklist: - timeline, - how manual overrides interact with fallback heuristics, - add guardrail to disallow force-pin during active autoscaling throttles, - change default TTL on routing locks, - CS comms log.

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by oncall: jin. Handoff planned to sara at 12:00 UTC for incident wrap and follow-up.

sara: taking over for post-incident checks. Jin — pls add the exact CLI commands and snapshots to the incident ticket. We'll also run a replay in staging to reproduce the loop.

jin: will add everything to REDWOOD-INC-472. Immediate impact mitigated. Next steps: triage root cause, backport guardrails, and coordinate with Runtime to drop the unsafe force-pin behavior.

maria: thanks everyone — good coordination. Keeping the banner up until we confirm stable metrics for 30m. :white_check_mark:
